label: US (FDA)
visualChecklist: Nutrition Facts panel uses the FDA format: boxed, bold "Nutrition Facts" heading, minimum type sizes (21 CFR 101.9(d))
Net quantity sits in the bottom 30% of the principal display panel, parallel to the base (21 CFR 101.105(f))
Net quantity type is at least the minimum height for the panel's area (21 CFR 101.105(h))
Product name (statement of identity) is a principal feature of the front panel, in bold type (21 CFR 101.3)
Ingredient list, allergen statement and manufacturer details are on the information panel, right of the front panel

rules.name: Disease claim
rules.aiGuidance: Flag wording that says or implies the product treats, cures, mitigates, manages or prevents a specific disease or medical condition (or a symptom of one), or that it is meant for people who have one. Foods and supplements that make these claims are regulated as drugs. Flag, for example: "helps manage diabetes", "lowers blood pressure", "prevents heart disease", "great for diabetics", "fights cancer", "relieves arthritis pain". Do NOT flag wording about supporting or maintaining normal, healthy body function that names no disease, condition or symptom. Those are structure/function claims, which this rule does not cover: "supports healthy blood sugar", "supports immunity", "builds strong bones", "supports heart health", "high protein". Tie-break: if the wording does not name a disease, condition or symptom, and does not say the product is for people who have one, do not flag it.

rules.name: No "Contains:" line (best practice)
rules.citation: FD&C Act §403(w)(1): an ingredient name that identifies the allergen satisfies the law; a "Contains:" statement is the alternative way to declare it

rules.name: Product name (statement of identity) missing
rules.citation: 21 CFR 101.3: the common or usual name of the food on the principal display panel
rules.explanation: No product name was found. The label must say what the food is, e.g. "Granola bites", on the front panel.
rules.advice: Add the product's common name to the front panel.

rules.name: Net quantity missing (metric and US units)
rules.citation: 21 CFR 101.105: net quantity of contents in both US customary (oz, fl oz, lb) and metric (g, ml) units
rules.explanation: No net quantity was found in both US customary and metric units, e.g. "Net wt. 1.4 oz (40 g)".
rules.advice: Add "Net wt. [oz] oz ([g] g)" to the bottom of the front panel.

rules.name: Ingredient list missing
rules.citation: 21 CFR 101.4: ingredients listed by common name in descending order of weight
rules.explanation: No ingredient list ("Ingredients: …") was found. Without it, allergens can't be checked either.
rules.advice: Add "Ingredients:" followed by every ingredient in descending order by weight.

rules.name: Nutrition Facts missing
rules.citation: 21 CFR 101.9: Nutrition Facts (or Supplement Facts for dietary supplements, 21 CFR 101.36)
rules.explanation: No Nutrition Facts (or Supplement Facts) panel was found in the text.
rules.advice: Paste the Nutrition Facts panel, or use Structured panels and fill in the Nutrition panel box.

rules.name: Name and place of business missing
rules.citation: 21 CFR 101.5: name and place of business of the manufacturer, packer or distributor
rules.explanation: No manufacturer, packer or distributor name and address was found.

fix.line: Distributed by: [company name, city, state, ZIP]

rules.name: Placeholder still on the label
rules.citation: 21 CFR 101.105 and 101.5: required declarations must state the real values
rules.explanation: This is a placeholder, not a real value. A required declaration with a placeholder is still missing.
rules.advice: Replace it with the real value (Fix all has a form for this).

rules.name: Nutrient claim without a nutrition line
rules.citation: 21 CFR 101.13: a nutrient content claim needs the nutrient's amount in the Nutrition Facts
rules.explanation: The label makes a nutrient claim, but the nutrition table has no line for that nutrient to back it up.
rules.advice: Add the Nutrition Facts with this nutrient's amount per serving, or remove the claim.

rules.name: Nutrient claim doesn't meet the FDA threshold
rules.citation: 21 CFR 101.54 (protein, fiber), 101.60 (sugar), 101.61 (sodium), 101.62 (fat): thresholds per reference amount
rules.explanation: The nutrition table doesn't support this claim's threshold.
rules.advice: Reformulate to meet the threshold, or use a weaker claim (e.g. "good source of") or none.
